subject: Acme POC — evaluation plan, success criteria, and shadow vs offline methodology
summary: Post-discovery follow-up to align on POC success criteria, evaluation methodology (offline evals vs online shadow), ownership, timeline, and next steps. Internal owners assigned and kickoff proposed.
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-10T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — suggested POC plan and evaluation approach

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion on the two primary evaluation goals: (1) verifying quality on your common intents and (2) understanding live performance under production traffic. Per our notes, attaching a draft POC plan (Acme_POC_plan.xlsx) with scope and timelines.

Quick recap & asks so we’re aligned:
- Success criteria (please confirm): intent classification match >= 95% on your labeled sample; latency p95 < 300ms for inference path; relevant response precision > 90% on the top-3 suggested responses.
- Evaluation approach: we recommend a two-phased evaluation — offline evals on your labeled test set to validate quality quickly, then a 2-week online shadow run (traffic mirroring) to measure latency, error rates, and real-user regressions.
- Ownership: Rachel to lead offline grading and evaluation harness; Marissa to own the online shadow run + rollout policy. I’ll own project coordination and the mutual action plan.
- Timeline (draft): kickoff Jan 18, offline evals Jan 19–24, rubric review Jan 25, online shadow Jan 26–Feb 8, wrap & decision Feb 10.

Next steps: please confirm success criteria and whether you prefer to run the shadow on a subset of traffic (and what %). Also confirm data access timeline (labeled test set + example logs).

Attachments: Acme_POC_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Dylan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-10T17:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — suggested POC plan and evaluation approach

Dylan — thanks for the follow-up and the plan. Priya and I reviewed. High-level thoughts:

- The success criteria you listed look reasonable. A couple of tweaks from our side: we want intent match >= 94% (we’ll accept 94 as floor) and we care a lot about regression on high-value intents (billing, cancellations) so would like per-intent pass thresholds.
- We prefer to run offline evals first (to fail fast) but strongly prefer the online shadow for at least 2 weeks on ~10% of traffic to capture latency and user-facing regressions. The shadow should be read-only (no user-visible responses).
- For cost modeling, can you add an estimated token-based cost projection to the POC plan? That will help our procurement team.

Availability: we can kickoff Jan 18 as proposed. We should have a labeled test set ready by Jan 16 (I’ll confirm with Priya).

Thanks — Alex
VP, Product
Acme Corp

Thanks — quick internal note and proposed rubric before we share final docs:

Proposed grading rubric (high level):
- Offline evals (automated): compare model outputs against labeled references using intent accuracy, top-k precision, and BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics for NLG quality. Score scale 0–100. Pass threshold: >= 80 overall, with no critical-intent below 85.
- Human review (sampling): for conversational/edge cases, human raters grade responses on correctness, safety, and helpfulness (1–5). Critical intents get a higher sampling rate.
- Online shadow metrics: latency p50/p95, error rate (exceptions/timeouts), live regression rate (measured via holdout ratio). Any significant regression (>3% absolute drop on a critical intent) triggers immediate rollback and postmortem.

Owner suggestions: Rachel = offline eval harness + automated grading; Marissa = shadow orchestration + dashboards; Dylan = mutual action plan and procurement liaison.

I’m attaching a draft eval rubric (acme_eval_rubric.md) with proposed score buckets and sample human-review templates. Can Rachel send the automation checklist and data access items to Alex/Priya?

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_eval_rubric.md (markdown)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-11T11:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — suggested POC plan and evaluation approach

Alex / Priya — happy to run the offline evals. Concrete asks from our side to unblock Jan 19 start:

1) Labeled test set: CSV with columns (user_utterance, intent_label, expected_response) — target size 3k examples, but we can work with a smaller initial set (~1k) for early signal.
2) Example traffic logs (anonymized) for sampling typical sessions.
3) Access: S3 read role or shared Drive folder where we can pull the test set and logs.

Rubric (excerpts from the attached md):
- Intent accuracy (weighted): critical intents weight 3, standard weight 1. Overall intent score = weighted_correct / weighted_total.
- Response precision (top-3): percent of top-3 suggestions that are relevant.
- Safety checks: automated filters and human spot-checks; any safety failure is a hard fail.
- Human sample: 200 sessions sampled across critical intents for manual rating (correct/helpful/safe).

Proposed timeline (confirmed with internal teams):
- Jan 16: Acme provides labeled set + logs access
- Jan 18: Kickoff call (10–11am PT)
- Jan 19–24: Offline evals run + rubric tuning
- Jan 25: Rubric review and decision on shadow parameters
- Jan 26–Feb 8: Online shadow (10% traffic)
- Feb 10: POC wrap and go/no-go decision

Next steps for us: I’ll create the eval harness repo and share readme + runbook by Jan 15. Dylan — can you confirm PO routing and who on procurement to loop in?

Thanks,
Rachel
Senior Product Manager, Evals
Redwood Inference
